study type: Network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
cohort: The study included data from 137 randomized trials comprising 87,466 women who received uterotonic drugs to prevent postpartum haemorrhage.
finding: Ergometrine plus oxytocin, carbetocin, and misoprostol plus oxytocin are more effective at preventing PPH (blood loss >= 500ml) compared to oxytocin, with carbetocin having a favorable side-effect profile similar to oxytocin.
mod_finding: Primary outcomes were stratified by mode of birth, and cost-effectiveness analyses were performed separately for vaginal births and caesarean sections, showing different cost-effectiveness profiles for various uterotonic strategies depending on the mode of delivery.
country: N/A (meta-analysis of international trials, copyright HMSO 2019 suggests UK affiliation but not study performance location)
